prefixes.actor_notes_at_this_call: Evidence: 736 paid rows across reset trajectories. Controlled pulse records 416–543 establish a zero-input baseline of −0.274723, −0.549447, then −0.824170; an initial unit x pulse shifts the first three outputs by −0.939181, a unit z pulse by −0.461237, while c alone has no effect. Amplitude scaling, x/z additivity, and x+c equivalence held for initial pulses. Delayed pulses in records 640–687, after four zeros, preserve the same x/z shifts over the next three outputs and then return to baseline. However, intended follow-up records 688–735 may again have been all-zero trajectories; this has not yet been checked from full rows. Many polynomial, latent recurrence, reservoir, kernel, tree, MLP/GRU and lag-summary candidates failed independent episode prediction. Two fitted polynomial submissions failed fresh confirmation (MSE 3.956 and 15.169); best cited cross-episode tree errors remain around 0.17, nowhere near the 1e−6 criterion. The sole evaluated model was fit on only the initial 192 rows and remains unsupported on newer evidence. Working hypothesis: simple pulse responses are linear/additive transient components, but broad control-history response remains unexplained. Next action is a small local check of exact controls, targets and target increments in the newest four trajectories; that proposed inspection has not happened yet. Keep 96 confirmation rows reserved.

Evidence: 736 paid rows across reset trajectories. Controlled pulses (rows 416–543) show zero-input output −0.274723, −0.549447, then −0.824170 steady; x=1 shifts outputs by −0.939181 for three steps, z=1 by −0.461237 for three, and c alone has no effect. Pulse effects scale linearly, x/z effects add, x+c matches x, and delayed pulses after four zeros reproduce the same three-step signatures (rows 640–687). Negative delayed x/z pulses reverse the shifts; delayed c has no effect; alternating x signs in rows 724–735 are consistent with overlapping three-step pulse contributions (inspection at run step 33). These controlled results support a compact additive transient response for isolated controls, but random-control trajectories remain unexplained. Multiple nonlinear, polynomial, latent-state, kernel, tree, MLP/GRU, and distributed-lag models have not generalized adequately; short-lag polynomial candidates failed fresh confirmation (MSE 3.956 and 15.169), and best cited episode-held-out tree error was ~0.17. Evaluated model fits only the initial 192 rows and has not been scored on current rows. Current action will compute leave-one-reset-trajectory-out and pooled error for affine FIR control histories at several lags; this detects whether isolated pulse response extends linearly to arbitrary mixed inputs, and whether to pursue interactions/state structure next. No new observation or model submission is being proposed.

Notebook: 1,552 paid response rows; 96 fresh confirmation rows are reserved, requiring MSE ≤1e-6. No candidate has passed. Two polynomial submissions failed fresh confirmation (MSE 3.956 and 15.169); many polynomial/FIR, latent-state, kernel, tree, neural, and autoregressive models had poor held-out-trajectory performance. Controlled records 416–735 show zero-input response −0.274723, −0.549447, then −0.824170; isolated x/z pulses shift three outputs by −0.939181/−0.461237 per unit, with tested linearity/additivity; c-only pulse and sustained controls were neutral in those conditions. Sustained x=.5, x=1, z=1 settle at −2.232942, −3.641714, −2.207882; pulse FIR broad-data MSE is 4.142. At fixed x=z=.5, steady output is −2.578870 for c≥−0.176 and +1.374835 for c≤−0.17625. Newer constant-input evidence (rows 1468–1551; inspected in steps 77–79) gives at x=z=.25: c=−.175 → −1.615038 and c=−.17625/−.1775 → +0.365935; at x=z=1: c=−.175 → −5.025426 and c=−.17625 → +4.187478. This appears to put the regime boundary in the same narrow interval for three diagonal amplitudes, contrary to earlier suggestion of a clear amplitude shift; it is not a general response law. Working hypothesis: a c-controlled regime change may be largely independent of amplitude for these x=z>0 settings, with regime-specific output scaling; alternatives include dependence on other control combinations/history. Proposed action (not yet run): summarize already-paid constant-control trajectories grouped by (x,z), listing c and steady output, to check whether boundary invariance holds beyond the three diagonal settings before designing a broader test.

Evidence: 1,664 paid response rows across 106 reset trajectories; 96 fresh rows are reserved and confirmation requires MSE ≤1e-6. No predictor has passed. Two polynomial submissions failed fresh confirmation (MSE 3.956 and 15.169); polynomial/FIR, latent-state, kernel, tree, neural and autoregressive approaches have generally remained inaccurate on whole-trajectory holdouts. Controlled records 416–927 show a zero-input transient, short additive x/z pulse effects, distinct sustained responses, and c-neutrality only in tested conditions. Sustained constant controls show a c-regime change near −0.176 across tested diagonal and off-diagonal settings, but this is not a general response law. Recent HGB holdout scores vary by feature construction: LOEO MSE 0.0441–0.130, with worst episodes 0.5–0.7; modest tuning at step 100 improved only to 0.1049 (worst 0.501). The current proposal tests a few lower-learning-rate/tree-capacity HGB settings using the same whole-reset-trajectory holdout and reports overall, worst-episode, and latest-episode errors. This is a computation-only diagnostic; no new observation or confirmation result is assumed. If scores remain far from confirmation accuracy, continue searching for a more appropriate dynamical representation rather than submit the candidate.
